findings.title: The `!DialogHost.IsOpen` check never takes effect, because of the order the `Loaded` handlers run in.**
findings.body:
**The `!DialogHost.IsOpen` check never takes effect, because of the order the `Loaded` handlers run in.**

`Loaded="Window_OnLoaded"` is attached inside `InitializeComponent()`, which runs in the constructor. `ViewManager.TryBindView` attaches `view.Loaded += async (_, _) => await viewModel.InitializeAsync()` only after the constructor returns. Routed-event handlers run in the order they were added, so this handler always runs **before** `MainViewModel.InitializeAsync()` has opened any dialog. That means `DialogHost.IsOpen` is always `false` here, and a hidden start always hides the window.

What happens next with `--start-hidden`:
- The Ukraine-support, dev-build and limited-gamma-range dialogs open inside a hidden window. Nobody sees them, but `InitializeAsync` waits on each one.
- `ShowGammaRangeMessageAsync` runs on **every** launch until the user unlocks the extended range. While it waits, `_checkForUpdatesTimer.Start()` is never reached, so the background update check stays off until the user opens the window and closes the dialog.
- Only `FinalizePendingUpdateAsync` handles this, because it calls `ShowActivateFocus()` itself.

Also, the window is shown by the lifetime and only then hidden in `Loaded`, so it can flash briefly on hidden startup. The code being reverted avoided both problems because it never showed the window.

Possible fixes: decide visibility inside `MainViewModel.InitializeAsync()` (show the window before each dialog, as `FinalizePendingUpdateAsync` does, and hide it otherwise). Or start the update timer before the dialog chain. Either way, the comment here should describe what the code actually does.

findings.title: `ShowSettingsCommand` is an `AsyncRelayCommand`. Calling `ICommand.Execute` directly skips the `CanExecute` gate (by default the command blocks concurrent runs). The command is still running while the
findings.body:
`ShowSettingsCommand` is an `AsyncRelayCommand`. Calling `ICommand.Execute` directly skips the `CanExecute` gate (by default the command blocks concurrent runs). The command is still running while the settings dialog is open, so it should be unavailable. But `DialogManager` serialises dialogs with a semaphore, so each extra click on the tray **Settings** item puts another settings dialog in the queue. Each one then pops up after the previous one is closed. The same happens if the user clicks it while a startup message box is open.

Suggest checking first:
```suggestion
        if (_mainViewModel.ShowSettingsCommand.CanExecute(null))
            _mainViewModel.ShowSettingsCommand.Execute(null);
```
This also restores the behaviour you get from the in-window settings button, which binds to the command and respects `CanExecute`.

findings.title: A `TwoWay` binding on `Window.IsVisible` works, but it is a bit fragile:
findings.body:
A `TwoWay` binding on `Window.IsVisible` works, but it is a bit fragile:
- `IsOpen` starts as `false`. When `ViewManager` assigns the `DataContext`, the binding writes `IsVisible = false` before the lifetime calls `Show()`. That does nothing today, but it relies on the lifetime calling `Show()` after the binding is set up.
- Writing `IsOpen = true` from the view model now *shows a window* (on `Window`, setting `IsVisible` calls `Show()`/`Hide()`). Nothing does that yet, but it is an easy-to-miss side effect for anyone who later treats `IsOpen` as a read-only status flag. Only the tray menu reads it.

If the binding exists only so the tray "Show/Hide" label stays correct, `Mode=OneWayToSource` says that intent more clearly and removes both edge cases.

result.result:
I reviewed PR #474 ("Revert UI unloading, restore persistent main window", already merged into `prime`) against its head commit `0603c3e`. I posted three inline comments; the summary below is the top-level review, which I couldn't post because the shell wasn't working.

## Inline comments

1. **`LightBulb/Views/MainView.axaml.cs:16` (correctness):** The `!DialogHost.IsOpen` check never takes effect. The XAML `Loaded` handler is attached in the window's constructor, before `ViewManager` attaches the one that starts `InitializeAsync()`. So the window is always hidden before any startup dialog opens. With `--start-hidden`:
   - The Ukraine-support, dev-build and gamma-range dialogs open inside the hidden window, where nobody sees them.
   - The gamma-range dialog runs on every launch until the user unlocks the extended range. While it waits, the 3-hourly update check (`_checkForUpdatesTimer`) never starts.
   - The window can also flash on screen before it hides.

   Only the pending-update dialog brings the window forward itself.
2. **`LightBulb/App.axaml.cs:144` (correctness, minor):** The tray **Settings** item calls `ShowSettingsCommand.Execute(null)` directly. That skips the command's check against running twice, and dialogs wait in a queue. So each extra click opens another settings dialog after the current one closes. I suggested checking `CanExecute` first.
3. **`LightBulb/Views/MainView.axaml:17` (maintainability):** The two-way `IsVisible` ↔ `IsOpen` binding means that setting `IsOpen` from the view model now shows or hides the window. It also briefly writes `false` before the window's first show. A one-way binding back to the view model (`OneWayToSource`) says the intent more clearly.

## Top-level observations
- **The revert is clean overall.** It brings back one window that hides instead of closing and removes the window-recreation code (`ShowMainWindow`, `WaitUntilLoadedAsync`, `App.Current`). The window stays loaded when hidden, so dropping `_isInitialized` and `WaitUntilLoadedAsync` is safe. `DashboardViewModel.InitializeAsync` can also run more than once safely.
- **Closing behaviour is right.** The window only cancels the close when the user closes it. Closes from app shutdown and OS shutdown still go through, so `Shutdown()` and logoff work without the explicit shutdown-mode setting.
- **Trade-off:** keeping the window in memory gives up the memory savings the reverted change was after. That's a reasonable choice, but the PR description should say so.
- **Security / performance:** no concerns.
- **Testing:** the only test projects cover `LightBulb.Core`, so none of this window logic is tested. Before merging, someone should manually test: starting hidden on first run, starting hidden with the gamma range still locked, double-clicking tray **Settings**, and Alt+F4 vs. tray **Exit**.
- **Docs:** no README change is needed.

**Caveats:**
- The local checkout is the PR's first commit (`354d65d`), not the head. I took the head code and line numbers from GitHub.
- The handler-order point is from reading the code. I didn't run the app to confirm it.
